blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Teaching humanoids loco-manipulation skills, such as carrying diverse objects, via visual imitation is a promising path toward generalist robots. However, collecting diverse, high-quality interaction videos, such as clips that clearly show a person’s full body and unoccluded interactions with objects, poses a practical barrier to scaling this approach. We propose PRISM, a real-to-sim-to-real framework that overcomes this limitation by amplifying a handful of real videos into a large, diverse training set. PRISM first generates hundreds of diverse “counterfactual” human–object interaction videos via video-to-video (V2V) generation from a few exemplar real videos. Our contact-anchored real-to-sim pipeline then reconstructs both human and object motions, retargeting this imperfect video data into physically plausible trajectories. The intra-class variability across these counterfactual videos lets us train a single policy that generalizes to unseen objects within each category. We demonstrate the full pipeline by deploying this policy on a real robot without any real-world fine-tuning. Using only onboard depth observations, our humanoid picks up, carries, and drops objects—including boxes, barrels, bins, and balls—across novel instances, sizes, and initial configurations.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: How can humanoids learn to interact with the diverse objects encountered in everyday life? Visual imitation learning offers a promising route: human demonstrations provide examples of the coordinated whole-body motions needed to approach, lift, carry, and drop various objects. Recent real-to-sim-to-real pipelines [ 1 ] have enabled humanoids to acquire contextual whole-body locomotion skills directly from human videos. These advances suggest a path toward generalist humanoids that learn a broad repertoire of locomotion and manipulation skills from internet-scale video data.
blocks.zh: 人造人如何学会与日常生活中遇到的各种物体相互作用? 视觉模仿学习提供了一条很有希望的路线:人类的演示提供了各种物体接近、抬起、携带和投放所需的协调全身运动的例子。 最近的真到真到真管[1]使得人造人能够直接从人视频中获得上下文的全身运动技能. 这些进步表明通俗主义人造物的途径是从互联网规模的视频数据中学习广泛的运动和操纵技能。

blocks.en: However, acquiring diverse, high-quality human–object interaction videos remains a practical bottleneck to scaling visual imitation. Internet videos are abundant, but their content and framing are shaped by human viewing preferences. Filtering Internet videos to find demonstrations that clearly show the person’s full body and how they interact with objects is therefore costly and impractical at scale. Yet, such interaction data does exist implicitly in modern video generative models [ 30 ] , whose learned priors over human motion and interactions can be used to synthesize diverse training videos.
blocks.zh: 然而,获取多样、高质量的人与物交互视频仍然是缩小视觉模仿的一个实际瓶颈。 互联网视频丰富多彩,但其内容和框架都是由人类取景偏好所塑造. 因此,过滤互联网视频以发现明显显示个人全身的演示,以及这些演示如何与物体互动,代价高昂,规模不切实际。 然而,这种互动数据在现代视频基因模型中确实隐含存在[30],其所学到的关于人类运动和互动的先入为出,可用于合成多种培训视频.

blocks.en: To address this data bottleneck, we propose PRISM , a real-to-sim-to-real framework that uses video-to-video (V2V) generation to expand a few real videos into diverse human–object interactions. We call these generated clips “counterfactual videos”: they depict interactions that did not occur in the source videos but could have occurred with different objects. From only four real-world videos of humans carrying boxes, we generate 256 counterfactual videos depicting the same task with boxes, balls, bins, and barrels of varying geometries and initial configurations. Our contact-anchored real-to-sim pipeline reconstructs human motion, the static scene, and dynamic object geometry and motion in a unified world frame, then retargets these imperfect reconstructions into physically plausible humanoid–object trajectories. With these trajectories, we train a single depth-based policy that picks up, carries, and drops unseen instances of these categories zero-shot in the real world, validating the full pipeline. Our policy also generalizes to categories absent from the generated videos (Fig. 1 ).

blocks.en: The core technical challenge is to obtain physically plausible robot demonstrations despite errors introduced by both counterfactual video generation and monocular reconstruction. Our key insight is to use contact signal as a shared constraint across reconstruction, retargeting, and policy learning. In the first reconstruction stage, human–object contact couples the two motions: human motion guides the object trajectory, while object contact helps correct errors in the reconstructed human pose. During the retargeting stage, sparse contact anchors specify where robot end-effectors should contact the object, guiding the refinement of noisy reconstructions into physically plausible robot–object trajectories while accommodating morphological differences. During policy learning, these anchors define contact rewards for a privileged teacher policy that co-tracks robot and object motion. We then distill it into a depth-based policy with joystick control for zero-shot sim-to-real deployment.
blocks.zh: 核心的技术挑战是,尽管反事实视频生成和单相机重建都出现了错误,但还是要取得实际可行的机器人演示。 我们的关键见解是使用联系信号作为重建、重新定位和政策学习的共同制约。 在第一个重建阶段,人类物体接触伴侣的两种动作:人类运动引导物体的轨迹,而物体接触有助于纠正被重建的人类姿势中的错误。 在重新瞄准阶段,稀少的接触锚规定了机器人最终影响器应在哪里与物体相接,引导将吵闹的重建精炼成物理上可行的机器人-物体轨迹,同时适应形态差异。 在政策学习期间,这些主播定义了一种特权教师政策的联系奖励,这种政策共同跟踪机器人和物体运动. 然后,我们把它提炼成一个深度政策 游戏棒控制 零镜头的模拟到现实的部署。

blocks.en: We summarize our contributions as follows: (1) We introduce a new learning paradigm that uses counterfactual video generation for scaling human–object interaction experience. (2) We propose a contact-anchored real-to-sim and retargeting pipeline that turns monocular reconstructions into physically plausible robot–object demonstrations. (3) We demonstrate the first real-to-sim-to-real pipeline that trains a unified whole-body humanoid policy that generalizes across diverse objects and enables joystick-controlled pick-up, carry, and drop behaviors from onboard depth observations.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Humanoid loco-manipulation has been widely studied in both computer graphics [ 28 , 7 ] and robotics [ 26 , 29 , 19 ] , where the goal is to coordinate whole-body locomotion and object interaction simultaneously. Some humanoid systems [ 26 ] learn interaction skills by tracking human motion references, but require dense reference motions or object trajectories during inference, limiting generalization to unseen objects and interaction configurations. More recent methods [ 9 , 4 , 18 ] reduce this dependency by learning more autonomous interaction policies from sparse goals or interaction-centric representations. Similarly, PRISM trains a unified whole-body humanoid policy that enables zero-shot joystick-controlled pick-up, carry, and drop behaviors from onboard depth observations, without reference or motion-capture systems during deployment.
blocks.zh: 在计算机图形[28,7]和机器人[26,29,19]中都广泛研究了人机操纵,目标是同时协调全身运动和物体交互. 一些人文系统[26]通过跟踪人类运动参考物来学习交互技能,但在推断时需要密集的参考运动或物体轨迹,将通论限制在看不见的物体和交互配置上. 较新的方法[9、4、18]通过从零星的目标或以互动为中心的表述中学习更自主的互动政策来减少这种依赖。 同样地,PRISM执行统一的全身人形政策,使得零发的游戏棒控制接取,携带,并放下从机上深度观测得到的行为,在部署时没有参考或动作抓取系统.

blocks.en: Recent works learn humanoid skills from human videos [ 26 , 10 ] , including terrain-aware locomotion via joint human–scene reconstruction [ 1 ] and dynamic object interactions [ 26 , 20 ] . However, capturing or curating diverse, high-quality interaction videos at scale remains challenging. PRISM addresses this complementary challenge by expanding a few real videos into diverse human–object interactions through video-to-video generation. With these data, we train a single policy that picks up, carries, and drops diverse objects zero-shot in the real world.

blocks.en:
Recent works have explored video generation for robot learning under two main paradigms.
One line uses video models as inference-time planners or action generators, synthesizing future visual rollouts to guide closed-loop manipulation [ 3 , 2 , 30 ] .
While such methods provide flexible visual reasoning, they require expensive test-time generation and may suffer from an executability gap between plausible videos and physically feasible robot actions.
Another line uses video models offline to synthesize robot demonstrations or augment robot datasets before policy learning [ 11 , 5 ] .
PRISM follows the offline-generation paradigm, but differs in generating counterfactual human interaction videos through grounded V2V generation rather than directly generating robot videos from text or images.
By conditioning on real demonstrations, V2V preserves realistic motion, lighting, and affordance-aware contacts, while a simple unified prompt can scale one exemplar into diverse object categories, poses, and intra-class variations by multiple sampling.
blocks.zh:
近期的作品探索了机器人在两大范式下学习的视频生成.
一行使用视频模型作为推断时间规划者或动作生成器,将未来的视觉展开合成来指导闭路操纵[3,2,30].
虽然这些方法提供了灵活的视觉推理,但它们需要昂贵的测试时间生成,并可能因假想视频与实际可行的机器人动作之间的可执行性差距而受到影响。
另一行使用下线视频模型在政策学习[11,5]前合成机器人演示或增强机器人数据集.
PISM遵循了离线生成范式,但在通过被禁用V2V生成反事实的人类互动视频方面有所不同,而不是直接从文本或图像生成机器人视频.
V2V通过对真实的演示进行调制,保留了现实运动,照明,和付得起的知觉接触,而简单的统一快取则可以将一个实例缩放成不同的对象类别,由多个采样构成,以及类内的变化.

blocks.en: 3 Real-to-Sim Data Acquisition
blocks.zh: 3 实到实 数据获取

blocks.en: Given a monocular video depicting a human interacting with a static scene and a dynamic object, our goal is to recover camera parameters ( K , { T i c } ) (K,\{T_{i}^{c}\}) , a static scene mesh M s M_{s} , a dynamic object with its metric mesh M o M_{o} and its per-frame poses { T i o } \{T_{i}^{o}\} , and 4D SMPL-X [ 12 ] motion, all in a unified world frame. Then we retarget the recovered data to humanoid–object trajectories for policy learning.

blocks.en: 3.1 Counterfactual Interaction Video Generation
blocks.zh: 3.1 反事实互动视频生成

blocks.en: Scaling real-to-sim learning with online videos remains challenging. Although internet videos are abundant, their content and framing are shaped by human viewing preferences. Filtering for diverse clips with clear full-body views, visible human–object interactions, and stable viewpoints is therefore costly and impractical at scale. We use video-to-video (V2V) generation to expand a small set of suitable real videos into diverse counterfactual interaction videos —interactions that did not occur in the source videos but could have occurred with different objects. Given a seed video and a category-level text prompt, we ask the model to replace the manipulated object while preserving the original background, lighting, camera viewpoint, and coarse task structure. This video conditioning grounds generation in a real scene and task while allowing object and human behavior to vary.
blocks.zh: 通过在线视频扩大真到真学习仍然具有挑战性。 虽然互联网视频数量众多,但其内容和框架都是由人类取景偏好所塑造的. 因此,过滤具有清晰的全体视图、可见的人体-物体相互作用和稳定观点的各种剪辑成本高昂,规模不切实际。 我们使用视频到视频(V2V)的生成,将一小组合适的真实视频扩展为各种反事实互动视频——这些互动在源视频中没有出现,但可能与不同对象发生. 鉴于种子视频和分类级文本提示,我们请模型在保留原始背景、照明、相机视角和粗糙的任务结构的同时替换被操纵的对象。 这种视频在真实的场景和任务中调节地面生成,同时允许物体和人的行为变化.

blocks.en: Importantly, the counterfactual variation is not limited to object geometry or appearance. When the object category, size, pose, or placement changes, the object’s manipulation affordances also change, and the human behavior adapts accordingly: the generated person may bend lower, adjust hand spacing, adapt the contact strategy based on the object’s affordances, or carry the object differently. Thus each generated clip provides an object-conditioned interaction strategy, rather than merely pairing the same human motion with a new object. This allows PRISM to obtain behavior-level variations in interaction data that are difficult to hard-code through geometry-level augmentation alone. Learning such adaptations from scratch would require exhaustive task-specific RL reward design; PRISM instead uses the video model as an offline prior over plausible human adaptations.
blocks.zh: 重要的是,反事实变化并不限于对象几何或外观. 当对象类别,大小,姿势,或位置发生变化时,对象的操控承受力也会发生变化,而人类的行为也会相应适应:生成的人可能弯下弯,调整手相,根据对象的承受力调整接触策略,或者以不同方式携带对象. 因此,每个生成的片段都提供了有对象条件的交互策略,而不是仅仅将同一个人类运动与一个新的物体配对. 这使得PISM能够单独通过几何级增强获得难以硬编码的相互作用数据中的行为级变化. 从零开始学习这种适应需要详尽无遗的针对特定任务的RL奖励设计;而PISM则使用视频模型作为人类在进行比合理适应之前的离线。

blocks.en: In practice, we record four real-world seed videos and use each as a grounded template for V2V generation. We prompt SeedDance 2.0 [ 15 ] to replace the manipulated object with a box, bin, barrel, or ball while preserving the original background, lighting, camera viewpoint, and temporal continuity (Appendix A ). Category-level prompts allow the model to vary object geometry, appearance, and pose while adapting human behavior accordingly. With 16 samples per category, each seed yields 64 counterfactual videos, expanding four real recordings into 256 videos for our real-to-sim pipeline.
blocks.zh: 在实践中,我们录制了四个真实世界的种子视频,每个视频都作为V2V生成的被禁用模板. 我们鼓励种子Dance 2.0 [15] 在保留原始背景、照明、相机视角和时间连续性(附录A.)的同时,将被操纵的物体取而代之。 分类级提示让模型在相应调整人类行为的同时,可以改变物体几何,外观,并摆出姿势. 每类16个样本,每个种子产生64个反事实视频,将4个真实录相扩展为256个视频,用于我们的真到真管.

blocks.en: 3.2 Contact-Anchored Real-to-Sim
blocks.zh: 3.2 联系人真实联系人

blocks.en: To imitate human motion from monocular video, we must disentangle it from camera-induced image motion and recover it in a consistent world coordinate frame. CRISP [ 23 ] integrates an human mesh recovery (HMR) network with visual SLAM to reconstruct a metrically-consistent human–scene–camera representation from monocular video, including camera intrinsics K ∈ ℝ 3 × 3 K\in\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3} , per-frame camera poses T i = [ R i ∣ t i ] ∈ S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) T_{i}=[R_{i}\mid t_{i}]\in SE(3) , a metric-scale scene point cloud P ~ \tilde{P} , and temporally aligned 4D human motion in a unified world coordinate frame. We use it as backend and extend it to reconstruct both the geometry and motion of dynamic objects. blocks.en: 4 Learning a Unified Visuomotor Interaction Policy
blocks.zh: 4 学习统一的维苏莫托人互动政策

blocks.en:
Using the reconstructed robot-object trajectories (details are in Appendix C ), our goal is to train a unified humanoid policy capable of pick-up, carry, and drop behaviors across diverse objects. The policy receives onboard depth observations and joystick commands, and autonomously performs object interaction behaviors conditioned on the perceived object geometry and placement.
Similar to prior visuomotor systems [ 27 , 6 ] , we adopt a two-stage training framework. We first train a privileged co-tracking teacher policy in simulation using full-state observations. We then distill this teacher into a unified depth-based student policy using a combination of DAgger [ 14 ] and reinforcement learning, enabling zero-shot sim-to-real deployment. An overview is shown in Fig. 2 .

使用被重建的机器人-物体轨迹(详情见附录C),我们的目标是训练一种能够跨越不同物体取取取、携带和降低行为的统一的人文政策。 策略接收了机上深度观测和活泼棒指令,自主地执行以所感知到的物体几何和位置为条件的物体交互行为.
与先前的机动系统[27,6]类似,我们采用两阶段培训框架。 我们首先在模拟中使用全州观测结果方面 训练一种特权的协同跟踪教师政策。 然后,我们利用Dagger[14]和强化学习的结合,将这位老师提炼成统一的深度学生政策,使零射成正向部署成为可能. 图2显示了概况。

blocks.en: 5 Results
blocks.zh: 5 结果

blocks.en: Overview. We demonstrate that humanoid robots can learn skills that generalize to diverse objects by imitating pure counterfactual generated videos. We first evaluate the effectiveness of our reconstructed data by comparing with the policy trained with OMOMO [ 7 ] data only. Next, we evaluate the real-world performance over 20+ diverse objects. Finally, we conduct necessary ablation study to validate the necessity of each module in our framework design. All evaluations are conducted in MuJoCo [ 17 ] under a sim-to-sim setting, except for Sec. 5.2 reports real-world robot experiments.
blocks.zh: 概览. 我们证明,人造机器人可以通过模仿纯反事实生成的视频来学习将各种物体概括化的技能. 我们首先通过仅与OMOMO[7]数据培训的政策进行比较,评估我们重建的数据的有效性。 接下来,我们评价现实世界的表现 超过20个不同的物体。 最后,我们进行必要的消化研究,以验证我们框架设计中每个单元的必要性。 所有评价均以"模拟"(sim-to-sim)设定在MujoCo [17]进行,但Sec 5.2报告真实世界的机器人实验除外.

blocks.en: 5.1 Reconstruction Quality from Real-to-Sim
blocks.zh: 5.1 从实到实的质量

blocks.en:
Evaluation Data. We process and filter OMOMO to retain 63 high-quality human–object interaction sequences, then double the data by adding an object-scaled variant for each sequence using OmniRetarget [ 29 ] .
This gives 126 sequences, with 90 for OMOMO-Train and 36 held out as OMOMO-Test .
For PRISM, the reported comparison uses an earlier student distilled from 80 teacher rollouts and evaluates 80 PRISM-ID interactions and 48 PRISM-OOD interactions with chairs, tables, lamps, and monitors. Appendix C distinguishes this evaluation from the updated training configuration.
blocks.zh:
评价数据。 我们处理和过滤OMOMO,以保留63个高质量的人-对象交互序列,然后通过使用OmniReoctarget[29]为每个序列添加一个对象尺度的变体来将数据增加一倍.
这提供了126个序列,其中90个用于OMOMO-Train,36个用于OMOMO-Test。
对PRISM来说,报告的比较利用了一名早期学生从80个教师推广中提取的精选,并评价了80个PRISM-ID互动和48个PRISM-OOD与椅子、桌子、灯具和监视器的互动。 附 录 C将这一评价与更新的培训配置区分开来.

blocks.en:
Evaluation Metrics. For the distilled student policy, we derive joystick commands from the reference motion and render depth observations in simulation to drive the policy.
A rollout is successful if the robot completes pick–carry–drop and places the object at the desired target position.
blocks.zh:
评价计量。 对于精炼出的学生政策,我们从参考运动中得出了"活泼"(joystick commands)指令,并在模拟中渲染出深度观测,以驱动政策.
如果机器人完成取出- 载入- 投放, 并且将物体放入理想的目标位置, 推出将成功 。

blocks.en: Discussion. OMOMO-trained policies perform well across OMOMO sequences, but transfer poorly to PRISM interactions, especially with out-of-domain objects. We identify three main failure modes: the policy struggles with unseen depth observations, overfits to close-range interactions and attempts to grasp before approaching distant objects, and fails to stabilize carry on novel object geometries. These failures suggest that OMOMO alone lacks the variation in perception, object configuration, and interaction dynamics required for robust loco-manipulation. In contrast, PRISM-trained policies generalize across both domains, demonstrating the broader transferability of PRISM data.
blocks.zh: 讨论。 OMOMO训练有素的政策在OMOMO序列中表现良好,但转而与PRISM的相互作用不佳,特别是与域外物体的相互作用。 我们确定了三种主要的失败模式:政策斗争用看不见的深度观测、过于适合近距离互动和试图在接近遥远物体之前抓住,以及未能稳定地进行新物体几何测量。 这些失败表明,光靠OMOMO缺乏强力机能操控所需的感知、对象配置和相互作用动态变化。 与此相反,经过PRISM培训的政策在两个领域都得到了普及,表明PRISM数据的可转让性更广。

blocks.en: 5.2 Real-World Deployment
blocks.zh: 5.2 实际世界部署

blocks.en: We deploy our controller at 50 Hz on a 29-DoF Unitree G1, with PD gains following [ 8 ] . A head-mounted D435i camera captures stereo images at 30 Hz, and Fast-FoundationStereo [ 24 ] estimates depth on an external computer connected to the robot via Ethernet. A human operator provides joystick commands. We freely place each object in front of the robot, varying its pose and distance across five trials. A trial succeeds if the robot reaches and grasps the object, then carries it stably for at least 3 m without dropping it or falling. We evaluate all test objects (Fig. 7 ) zero-shot, without using their scans or reconstructions for training. Videos are available on our project website .
blocks.zh: 我们把控制器部署在50赫兹 29-DOF Unitree G1上,PD增收跟随[8]. 一台头架的D435i相机在30Hz拍摄到立体图像,而"快取"(Fast-FoundationStereo [24])则估计出通过以太网连接到机器人的外部计算机上的深度. 人类操作员提供活泼棒指令. 我们自由地将每个物体置于机器人面前,在五次试验中改变其姿势和距离。 如果机器人到达并抓住物体,试验就成功,然后将物体用至少3米刺入而不会掉入或掉入. 我们评价所有测试对象(图7)零发,不使用他们的扫描或重建训练. 视频可在我们的项目网站上查阅。

blocks.en: Discussion. We find that Fast-FoundationStereo substantially reduces the depth sim-to-real gap. We manually tilt the neck about 10 ∘ 10^{\circ} upward from its default position, relying on camera-pose randomization during training to tolerate imprecise calibration. During bending, the neck sometimes resets to default or deviates from its target angle, producing out-of-distribution depth observations.
blocks.zh: 讨论。 我们发现"快进基金会"(Fast-FoundationStereo)大大地缩小了深度-正对-现实差距. 我们手动将颈部从默认位置上向上倾斜约10----10--Circ],依靠相机在训练时的随机化来容忍不精确的校正. 在弯曲过程中,颈部有时会重新设置默认或偏离目标角度,产生分流外深度观测.

blocks.en: 5.3 Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 5.3 读取研究

blocks.en: Using eight seeds at submission, V2V outperforms geometric augmentation with fewer demonstrations (80 vs. 103; Appendix F ). We then ablate the key real-to-sim-to-real components on this expanded dataset. Figure 4 separately visualizes the initial object poses of 137 generated clips and four real-video seeds. Following [ 23 ] , a good reconstruction for robot learning should be physically plausible, simulatable and useful for policy training. Therefore, we use the reconstructed trajectories to train policies in simulation, and report the downstream task success rate as the main metric. We define the baseline as: initialize object geometry and poses by SAM3D [ 16 ] , then track it by FoundationPose [ 25 ] , and retarget it into simulation-ready robot–object demonstrations with OmniRetarget [ 29 ] . Table 3 shows that better real-to-sim data directly benefits downstream policy learning. The baseline produces inaccurate robot–object interactions that limit effective policy learning. Anchored object pose and contact-aware retargeting progressively improve the data quality thus lead to stronger downstream performance. The contact reward further improves the policy by encouraging stable, task-relevant robot–object contacts during teacher and student training.
blocks.zh: V2V在提交时使用8个种子,比几何增生效果好,演示次数较少(80对103;附录F)。 然后,我们放弃了这个扩展数据集上的关键真实到真实的组件。 图4分别可视化了137个生成的片段和4个真视频种子的初始对象外观. 在[23]之后,对机器人学习进行良好的重建应该从物理上讲是可信的,可以模拟的,并且有助于政策培训。 因此,我们利用重建的轨迹来训练模拟政策,并将下游任务的成功率作为主要衡量标准。 我们把基线定义为:初始化物体几何并用 SAM3D [16] 来定位,然后用 FoundationPose [25] 来跟踪它,并将其重新定位为模拟准备的机器人-物体演示,使用 OmniReobject [29] 。 表3显示,更好的实到实数据直接有利于下游的政策学习。 基线产生不准确的机器人-对象相互作用,限制了有效的政策学习。 确定对象的姿势和接触意识的重新定位逐步提高数据质量,从而增强下游的性能。 联系奖励通过鼓励在师生培训期间稳定、与任务相关的机器人-对象接触,进一步改善了政策。

At scale, heterogeneous-asset setup in Isaac Lab limits simulation and training throughput. Training on elevated V2V data may extend this range.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented PRISM , a real-to-sim-to-real framework that expands a few real videos into diverse humanoid demonstrations.
Contact-anchored reconstruction and retargeting turn imperfect counterfactual videos into physically plausible robot–object trajectories.
The resulting unified depth-based policy picks up, carries, and drops unseen objects zero-shot in the real world.
These results highlight video generation as a practical data source for generalizable whole-body interaction.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了PISM, 一个真实到真实的框架,
将不完美的反事实视频转换成物理上可行的机器人-物体轨迹。
由此而来的统一深度政策在现实世界中拾起,携带,并放下了看不见的物体零发.
这些结果凸显出视频生成是一个实用的数据源,用于通俗的全身-身体交互.

blocks.en: 7 Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 7 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en: Our pipeline delivers encouraging real-world results, yet several practical weaknesses remain.
blocks.zh: 我们的管道能够产生令人鼓舞的现实世界成果,但仍然存在若干实际弱点。

blocks.en:
Reconstruction and Retargeting. Monocular 4D human–object–scene recovery remains challenging, especially when preserving consistent contacts and interaction dynamics.
Reconstruction errors can propagate through retargeting and compromise robot demonstrations.
Although Astra was unavailable during the development of this work, such coding agents could automate and iteratively refine reconstruction from counterfactual videos.
Combining these agents with contact-aware retargeting and simulation-based validation may improve the reliability of robot demonstrations.
blocks.zh:
重建和重新瞄准目标。 单相机4D的人体-物体-场景恢复仍然具有挑战性,特别是在保持持续接触和互动动态时。
重建错误可以通过重新瞄准和妥协机器人演示来传播。
虽然在这项工作的开发过程中Astra是没有的,但这种编码代理可以自动化并迭代地从反事实视频中完善重建.
将这些物剂与接触感再定向和以模拟为基础的验证相结合,可以提高机器人演示的可靠性.

blocks.en: Data Scale. Four seed videos yield 256 generated clips, 137 feasible trajectories, and 129 successful teacher rollouts. This scale is insufficient to characterize scaling behavior, with reconstruction and retargeting remaining practical bottlenecks. Future work should jointly scale generation and trajectory recovery to study how demonstration quantity and quality affect zero-shot generalization.
blocks.zh: 数据缩放. 4个种子视频产生256个出品剪辑,137个可行的轨迹,129个教师成功推出. 这一规模不足以描述规模化行为,无法重建并重新确定剩余的实际瓶颈。 今后的工作应当联合规模化生成和轨迹回收,以研究示范数量和质量如何影响零发通化。

blocks.en: Object Physics. We use category-specific nominal masses and mesh-derived inertias, with coupled mass–inertia scaling and randomized friction (Appendix E ). We do not identify instance-specific surface properties or internal mass distributions, which can cause sim-to-real contact mismatch.
blocks.zh: 物体物理. 我们使用特定类别的名义质量和网状衍生惯性,并伴有质量-惰性缩放和随机摩擦(附录E). 我们没有识别出特定实例的表面属性或内部质量分布,这可能造成sim-to-real的接触不匹配.

blocks.en: Simulation Limitations. We model dynamic objects as rigid bodies. Thus the policy can struggle with articulated or deformable objects whose contact geometry may change during interaction. For example, foldable chairs may shift through internal joints, causing unstable grasps or loss of control.
blocks.zh: 模拟限制。 我们把动态物体模拟为刚性的身体. 因此,该政策可以与那些在互动过程中接触几何可能发生变化的被阐明或可变形物体相抗衡。 例如可折叠椅可能通过内部关节转动,导致抓取不稳定或失去控制.

blocks.en: Appendix A Counterfactual Video Generation Details
blocks.zh: 附录 A 反事实视频生成细节

blocks.en: We record four real-world seed videos of humans carrying boxes, selecting clips with clear full-body views, limited occlusion, and stable viewpoints. Using the SeedDance 2.0 web interface [ 15 ] , we condition generation on each seed video and a category-level text prompt. The prompt replaces the manipulated object while preserving the background, lighting, camera viewpoint, and coarse task structure. These counterfactual videos depict interactions that could have occurred with different objects, allowing both object properties and human behavior to vary.
blocks.zh: 我们记录了四个真实世界的种子视频 人类携带箱子, 选择的片段 清晰的全身视图, 有限的隔离, 稳定的观点。 使用"种子Dance 2.0"网页界面[15],我们在每个种子视频上附加生成条件和一个分类级文本提示. 提示取代被操纵的对象,同时保留背景,照明,相机视角,和粗糙的任务结构. 这些反事实视频描绘了可能与不同物体发生的相互作用,使得物体属性和人类行为都有所不同.

blocks.en: We generate 16 samples for each of four categories—boxes, bins, barrels, and balls—per seed video. This yields 64 counterfactual videos per seed and 256 videos in total. All generated videos are subsequently processed by our contact-anchored real-to-sim pipeline.
blocks.zh: 我们为每只种子录像的四类——箱、桶、桶和球——生成16个样本。 这样,每个种子产生64个反事实录像,256个录像。 所有生成的视频随后都由我们的联系人安心的实到实的管道处理.

blocks.en: Prompt template. Figure 6 shows the shared template. We instantiate <CLS> with a target object category without specifying an individual instance’s geometry, size, or pose, allowing the video model to generate variation within each category and adapt the human interaction accordingly.
blocks.zh: 快速模板 。 图6显示共享模板。 我们用目标对象类别即时化“CLS”而不指定单个实例的几何、大小或外观,使视频模型能够在每个类别内产生变化,并相应调整人类互动。

blocks.en: Figure 6: Video-to-video prompt template. <VIDEO> denotes the seed video, and <CLS> specifies a box, bin, barrel, or ball. The highlighted instruction changes the manipulated object while allowing the human interaction to adapt.
blocks.zh: 图6:视频到视频即时模板. < VIDEO> 表示种子视频, < CLS> 指定一个框、 bin、 桶或球。 被突出显示的指令会改变被被操纵的对象,同时允许人类的相互作用适应.

blocks.en: Appendix B Real-World Test Objects
blocks.zh: 附录B 真实世界测试对象

blocks.en: We test unseen instances from the four generated object categories and objects from categories absent from the counterfactual videos (Fig. 7 ). No scans or reconstructions of these real-world test objects are used for training. Following Sec. 5.2 , each object is tested in five trials with varied initial poses and distances. A trial succeeds if the robot reaches and grasps the object, then carries it stably for at least 3 m without dropping it or falling. Table 2 reports the resulting success rates.
blocks.zh: 我们从四个生成的对象类别中测试未见的实例,从反事实视频中没有的类别中测试未见的实例(图7)。 没有对这些现实世界的测试对象进行扫描或重建来进行训练. 继第5.2条之后,每个物体在五个试验中进行测试,其初始姿势和距离各不相同。 如果机器人到达并抓住物体,试验就成功,然后将物体用至少3米刺入而不会掉入或掉入. 表2报告了由此产生的成功率。

blocks.en: Figure 7: Real-world test objects. In-domain objects are unseen instances of boxes, bins, barrels, and balls. Out-of-domain objects belong to categories absent from the generated training videos. Both groups vary in appearance, geometry, weight, and scale.
blocks.zh: 图7:真实世界测试对象. 域内物体是未见的盒子、桶、桶和球等实例。 域外对象属于所生成的培训视频未包含的类别. 这两个组在外观,几何,重量,和尺度上都各不相同.

blocks.en: Appendix C Training Data and Simulation Evaluation
blocks.zh: 附录C 培训数据和模拟评价

blocks.en: Reconstruction and retargeting. Of the 256 generated videos, 137 yield feasible robot–object trajectories through contact-anchored reconstruction and retargeting. The remaining sequences fail the constrained solver, mainly because of severe collisions. In particular, some generated objects are too large for the Unitree G1 humanoid to carry without object–body collisions.
blocks.zh: 重建和重新瞄准目标。 在制作的256个视频中,137个通过接触障碍的重建和重新瞄准而产生可行的机器人-物体轨迹。 所剩的序列会使受约束的解析器出故障,这主要是因为严重的相撞. 特别是,一些产生的物体太大,Unitree G1人体无法携带,无法不发生物体-身体相撞。

blocks.en: We train the privileged co-tracking teacher on these 137 trajectories for 40K iterations and obtain 129 successful teacher rollouts. These rollouts provide the robot and object motion references for student distillation, replacing the original kinematic trajectories with interactions executed in simulation. We train the unified depth-based student for 28K iterations using this set of 129 demonstrations.
blocks.zh: 我们为这137个轨迹培训特权联合跟踪教师,用于40K迭代,并获得129个成功的教师推广。 这些推出为学生蒸馏提供了机器人和物体运动参考,用模拟中执行的相互作用来取而代之的原始动能轨迹. 我们利用这组129次示威来训练28K次迭代的统一深度学生。

blocks.en: Reported evaluation setting. The cross-domain results in the main paper use an earlier student distilled from 80 successful rollouts of a 20K-iteration teacher checkpoint. Its PRISM-ID evaluation set comprises these 80 interactions. These results correspond to the earlier training configuration; results for the updated student trained on 129 demonstrations are not included in that comparison.
blocks.zh: 报告的评价设置。 主论文的跨域取出结果使用一名较早的学生从一个20K的教师检查站的80个成功推出中分出. 它的PRISM-ID评价集包括这80个互动. 这些结果与先前的培训配置一致;在129个示威中接受培训的更新学生的结果不包括在比较中。

blocks.en: Simulation evaluation data. For the OMOMO comparison, we retain 63 human–object interaction sequences and add an object-scaled variant of each using OmniRetarget [ 29 ] . The resulting 126 sequences are split into 90 training sequences and 36 held-out test sequences. We additionally reconstruct 48 PRISM out-of-domain interactions, with 12 instances each from tables, chairs, lamps, and monitors. These held-out categories are absent from the generated training data.
blocks.zh: 模拟评价数据. 就OMOMO比较而言,我们保留了63个人与对象的相互作用序列,并使用OmniRetarget[29]添加了每个对象的标定变体. 由此产生的126个序列被分为90个训练序列和36个被搁置的测试序列. 此外,我们重建了48个PRISM域外互动,从桌子、椅子、灯和监视器中各有12个实例。 所产生的培训数据中没有这些被搁置类别。

blocks.en: Simulation evaluation protocol. We evaluate the distilled student in MuJoCo [ 17 ] , rendering depth observations and deriving joystick commands from the reference motion. Success requires completing pick–carry–drop and placing the object at the desired target position. This simulation metric includes the final placement, whereas the real-world metric above measures reaching, grasping, and stable carrying over at least 3 m.
blocks.zh: 模拟评价协议. 我们评估了穆乔科的蒸馏学生 [17] , 进行深度观测并从参考运动中得出了乐杆指令。 成功需要完成 pick- carry- drop 和将对象放入理想的目标位置 。 这一模拟衡量标准包括最后位置,而实际世界衡量标准高于衡量标准,达到、掌握和稳定地结转至少3米。

blocks.en: Both teacher and student policies use 3-layer MLPs and are trained for 40K and 28K iterations, respectively. Each stage runs 4096 environments per GPU on 8 NVIDIA L40S GPUs (32,768 environments in total). Tables 4 – 6 report observations, rewards, and hyperparameters. Object physics and payload sensitivity are detailed in Appendix E .

blocks.en: Depth observations and deployment. The student actor receives proprioception, joystick commands, and onboard depth. Joystick commands specify a relative planar root position and yaw, together with a binary drop command. During training, these are derived from the reference root trajectory and carry-end time. Depth is encoded by a small CNN into a 32-dimensional feature. At deployment, Fast-FoundationStereo [ 24 ] runs on an external computer linked to the robot via Ethernet, estimating depth from the head-mounted D435i stereo images. We find that this substantially reduces the sim-to-real gap in depth observations. The camera operates at 30 Hz and the policy at 50 Hz; the student transfers zero-shot without reference motion or external motion capture.

blocks.en: Distillation and initialization. We combine DAgger imitation with PPO, progressively increasing the PPO coefficient and retaining λ = 0.9 \lambda=0.9 during the final 20K iterations. Successful teacher rollouts supply the motion references. We first train a student for 23K iterations using the same method on box-only data. We then restore only its actor weights, leaving the critic and optimizer freshly initialized, and train for 28K iterations on boxes, bins, barrels, and balls. Training from scratch also succeeds; warm starting accelerates convergence and is used for our released checkpoint. We randomize camera pose and corrupt depth with noise, dropout, holes, edge artifacts, and offsets.

blocks.en: Contact rewards. Both teacher training and the student’s PPO objective use object-frame contact anchors from reconstruction and retargeting. Rewards encourage reaching these targets with sufficient contact force. Table 5 lists the teacher reward weights and scales.

blocks.en: For two-handed carrying, 2D overlap gives contact timing; mesh intersections with the segment between palm centers give object-frame anchors (Sec. 3.2 ). Pose/mesh errors can cause penetration and IK failure. We retain non-penetrating IK solutions and full-trajectory teacher rollouts (Appendix C ), without formal contact or feasibility guarantees.
